titulo: Context in bands: 50, 70 and 85% of the compaction point
lead: The biggest enemy of a long session is repeated compaction: the goal survives, but what is done and what remains get diluted. The hook-longrun measures the context and acts before the limit, in three bands. In this lesson you turn on the hook and trigger all three bands in a rehearsal, without spending a token.
objetivo: turn on the hook-longrun and trigger the three bands in a rehearsal, knowing what each one asks of the agent and when to do /clear + /prime.

aprende.t: Where the bands sit: ~484, ~677 and ~822 thousand tokens
Compaction × handoff: what each one keeps
Turn on the hook for the five Claude Code events
Rehearse the hook with a fake transcript

hero_alt: Industrial pressure gauge with the needle in the middle band on a dark panel.

secoes.titulo: The bands over the compaction point
secoes.sub: The percentage is of the point at which Claude Code compacts by size, not of the whole window.

nos.detalhe: The hook asks the agent to write in canal.md what it would need if the history disappeared right now: facts, lessons, glossary, pitfalls, where things are. Then work continues as normal. It only shows up with a long run active.

Update state, progress and canal, finish the current unit of work, write the handoff without waiting to be asked, and tell you it is time for /compact. Compacting early summarizes better than the automatic one near the limit. In any session (even without a longrun), this band asks for the handoff.

Do not open new work. Update the state and ask for /session-handoff, a new session and /prime at the end of the unit in progress, without dropping it midway. With no human around, continue only to the next checkpoint.

itens.t: Afterward: reread the folder and the handoff

nos.detalhe: Documented Claude Code point for 1M models (CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW or LONGRUN_TETO change it). After compacting, the hook tells the agent to reread goal → state → plan → canal and this session's handoff. On the 3rd compaction: continue the task in progress and suggest a new session when it finishes.

secoes.legenda: Hook-longrun 1.9.6 (10/18/2026). The bands change with LONGRUN_FAIXAS="50,70,85". The warning arrives one tool call later, because the transcript is written with a delay.
secoes.dica: In the measurements from 10/07 to 10/15/2026, no session compacted by size: all 93 compactions were due to idle time (lesson 4).

secoes.titulo: Compact, write a handoff, or open a new session
secoes.sub: What each path keeps, measured on 10/15/2026 (17 compactions with a handoff from the same session in the 3 h before).

texto: The summary cites 20 to 54 files and keeps recent steps and commands. Within the same session, it holds more concrete detail than the handoff.
But it doesn't separate what's confirmed from what's a guess, it mixes the decisions into the narrative, and it doesn't survive /clear.
It cites 1 to 27 files, but it marks what was proven, and keeps the decisions and the next action in a section of their own.
It's the only one that works for another session, another day, or Codex. The two together are better than either one alone.

exemplo.texto: Writing the handoff from the compaction summary: it becomes a copy of a copy.

texto: The new session rediscovers things: 80% of the first 25 steps were reads, versus 51–59% after compacting.
That's why the new session comes at band 3 or the 3rd compaction, at the end of the unit in progress, and not early.
Half of a 1.84 GB JSONL measured on 10/01/2026 was tool output. Write logs to a file and read the part you need (tail -50).
A subagent spends its own context and returns only the summary; Anthropic cites returns of 1,000 to 2,000 tokens. How to use subagents is the topic of course 3.

secoes.titulo: Turn on the hook and rehearse the bands
secoes.sub: The rehearsal writes a fake transcript with whatever number of tokens you want and calls the hook the way Claude Code would.

blocos.rot: ensaio-hook.sh · save to a file and run with bash
blocos.conteudo:
# ensaio-hook.sh — dispara o hook-longrun com uma transcrição FALSA (nenhum token gasto)
# uso: bash ensaio-hook.sh <tokens|-> [minutos-parado] [evento]     ("-" reaproveita a transcrição anterior)
E=/tmp/ensaio-hook; K=~/projetos/execucao-longa
mkdir -p $E/proj/longrun/2026-10-19-teste $E/proj/handoffs/history
[ -f $E/proj/longrun/2026-10-19-teste/state.md ] || echo "# Estado" > $E/proj/longrun/2026-10-19-teste/state.md
[ "${1:-500000}" = "-" ] || python3 - "${1:-500000}" "${2:-0}" > $E/t.jsonl <<'PY'
import json, sys, time, datetime
n, parado = int(sys.argv[1]), float(sys.argv[2])
ts = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(time.time() - parado * 60, datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
print(json.dumps({"type": "assistant", "timestamp": ts, "message": {"model": "claude-opus-5-5",
      "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "ok"}],
      "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "cache_read_input_tokens": n - 10, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0}}}))
PY
echo "{\"hook_event_name\":\"${3:-PostToolUse}\",\"cwd\":\"$E/proj\",\"session_id\":\"ensaio\",\"transcript_path\":\"$E/t.jsonl\",\"prompt\":\"oi\"}" \
  | LONGRUN_ESTADO=$E/estado LONGRUN_AGENDAR_ARQ=$E/agenda.jsonl python3 $K/tools/hook-longrun.py
echo

rm -rf /tmp/ensaio-hook
bash ensaio-hook.sh 500000    # faixa 1
bash ensaio-hook.sh 500000    # mesma faixa: silêncio (uma vez por faixa)
bash ensaio-hook.sh 700000    # faixa 2
bash ensaio-hook.sh 830000    # faixa 3

Line breaks and (…) added to fit the screen; the text is from hook-longrun 1.9.6. The additionalContext goes to the agent; the systemMessage appears to you.

• There is no compaction hook or counter. Track the percentage in /status; what follows the bands is the AGENTS.md rule (lesson 1) and you.
  • Measured in the kit: Codex compacts near 90–93% of the window, around 230–240 thousand of 258 thousand, too late for good summary quality. Do the manual /compact earlier.
  • With an OpenAI model, automatic compaction runs on the server and ignores the compact_prompt; the structured prompt in ~/.codex/config.toml only applies to the manual /compact.

secoes.sub: The first exercise touches your settings.json: make a backup first.

exercicios.titulo: E6 · Hook turned on for all five events
exercicios.texto: Copy settings.json to settings.json.bak and merge the hooks excerpt into the ones you already have (don't delete yours). Open a new Claude Code session to load it.
exercicios.pronto: python3 -c "import json,os;h=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/settings.json')))['hooks'];print(sorted(e for e,l in h.items() if 'hook-longrun' in json.dumps(l)))" → ['PostToolUse', 'PreCompact', 'SessionStart', 'Stop', 'UserPromptSubmit'].

exercicios.titulo: E7 · The three bands in the rehearsal
exercicios.texto: Save ensaio-hook.sh and run the three-band sequence. Then delete /tmp/ensaio-hook and run LONGRUN_TETO=600000 bash ensaio-hook.sh 500000.
exercicios.pronto: these appear, in this order: FAIXA 1 de 3, nothing, FAIXA 2 de 3, and FAIXA 3 de 3; with LONGRUN_TETO=600000, 500 thousand already lands in FAIXA 2 de 3 (83% of 600 thousand).

perguntas.p: On a 1M model, at how many tokens does the hook warn for band 2 by default?
perguntas.explica: The calculation is based on the compaction point by size (~967 thousand), not on the window. The 112/157/191 thousand bands were from hook 1.2.x, which used the wrong cap of 225 thousand and fired in the middle of the work.

perguntas.p: Band 3 fired in the middle of a refactor. What should the agent do?
opcoes: Finish the unit in progress without opening new work; when it's done, handoff + new session
Ignore it: it's just a warning
Delete canal.md to free up context
Drop the refactor right away, write the handoff and ask for /clear to open a clean new session
perguntas.explica: Since 1.4.1, band 3 and the 3rd compaction no longer tell you to drop everything midway: the new session costs more to read (80% of the first 25 steps), so it comes at the end of the unit.

perguntas.p: Within the same session, which one keeps more concrete detail (files, steps)?
opcoes: The handoff, which separates proven from guessed
perguntas.explica: Measured on 10/15: the summary cites 20–54 files; the handoff, 1–27. The handoff wins at separating proven from guessed, at decisions, and at surviving /clear. That's why you use both together.

perguntas.p: You use Codex. How do you follow the bands?
opcoes: Watches the % in /status and follows the AGENTS.md rule, with a manual /compact before 90%
By setting compact_prompt in config.toml, which Codex applies on every automatic compaction
perguntas.explica: Codex has no compaction hook and no counter. The written rule and you play the role of the hook; and its automatic compaction ignores the compact_prompt with an OpenAI model.

itens.texto: The bands are 50/70/85% of ~967k: canal, then state + handoff + /compact, then nothing new and a new session at the end.
The compaction keeps more detail; the handoff keeps what's proven and the decisions, and survives /clear.
With a fake transcript you see every hook warning without spending a single token.
